intended_object: For an affine algebraic group G = Spec H over an algebraically closed field k, a finite-dimensional representation (comodule) M and a line [m] ∈ P(M), this is the automorphism of the orbit G·[m] ⊂ P(M) given by translation by a rational point g ∈ G(k). The orbit carries its locally closed scheme-theoretic image structure. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation (Milne, Algebraic Groups §7).
explanation:
The forward map is the unique endomorphism of the orbit scheme whose composite with the orbit immersion ι equals ι followed by ambient projective translation by g. It exists because the orbit map G → orbit is surjective and scheme-theoretically dominant, and ι is an immersion, so the lifting property applies. The inverse map is the same lift built from g⁻¹. Both identities are checked by cancelling the monomorphism ι, using that projective translation by g⁻¹ is the inverse of translation by g.

So this is exactly the restriction of the projective action of g to the orbit. It is an isomorphism, and the library goes on to prove that it is compatible with group multiplication and the identity, commutes with the orbit map and left translation, and lies over Spec k.

The hypotheses (k algebraically closed, H of finite type, M finite-dimensional, m unimodular) are copied from the definition of `projectiveOrbitScheme`, the locally closed orbit that this map acts on. The definition does not narrow that setting any further. Mathlib has no counterpart for orbit schemes of algebraic group representations.
